rows.question: How far apart, by date, were the first lunar touchdown and the first step onto the surface?
rows.answer:
The first lunar touchdown and the first step onto the surface were one day apart, by date.

- **Touchdown:** The Eagle lunar module landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility. [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **First step:** Neil Armstrong was the first person to step onto the lunar surface, on 1969-07-21 UTC. [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes give only dates, not times, so the gap is one calendar day (in UTC). They do not give the hours of either event.

[stated] First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)

rows.question: The flight surgeon's worry led to an astronaut being removed from a crew. Which mission did that astronaut later fly, and who commanded it?
rows.answer:
The astronaut is Ken Mattingly. Flight surgeon Charles Berry worried that Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Flight surgeon Charles Berry worried Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". His Apollo 13 command module pilot assignment was changed on 1970-04-10 [[ken-mattingly]] "[stated] Assigned to Apollo 16 as command module pilot (was Apollo 13 command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

He later flew Apollo 16 [[ken-mattingly]] "[stated] Assigned to Apollo 16 as command module pilot (was Apollo 13 command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". Apollo 16's crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke [[apollo-16]] "[stated] Crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

Apollo 16 was commanded by John Young [[john-young]] "[stated] Commander of Apollo 16 (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

rows.answer: Aldrin's Gemini flight came first. He flew Gemini 12 in 1966 [[buzz-aldrin]] "[stated] Flew Gemini 12 in 1966 (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". The first Saturn V launch was the uncrewed Apollo 4 flight on 9 November 1967 [[saturn-v]] "[stated] First launched uncrewed on Apollo 4 on 1967-11-09 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The notes give only the year for Gemini 12, so the order rests on 1966 versus 1967.

rows.question: What did the AS-204 tragedy lead to?
rows.answer:
The AS-204 tragedy (the Apollo 1 cabin fire) led to a command module redesign that included a quick-opening hatch. [[apollo-1]] "[stated] Led to a command module redesign that included a quick-opening hatch (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The fire happened during a launch rehearsal on 1967-01-27 and killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee. [[apollo-1]] "[stated] A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: Who does the brain record as having a part in the Apollo 13 crew swap, and what was each person's part?
rows.answer:
**Charlie Duke** started the crew swap. He was the backup lunar module pilot, and he exposed the crews by catching German measles. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". He caught it from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before launch. [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

**Ken Mattingly** was removed from the crew. Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed he had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". He never contracted German measles. [[ken-mattingly]] "[stated] Never contracted German measles (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

**Jack Swigert** replaced him. He had been the backup command module pilot and became the prime command module pilot. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". He was immune to rubella, which made him eligible to fly. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was immune to rubella, which made him eligible to fly (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

**Charles Berry** was a flight surgeon who worried that Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Flight surgeon Charles Berry worried Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". The brain has no note for Berry.

The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced on 1970-04-10. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". The brain does not name the individuals at that meeting.

rows.question: The craft whose engine put Apollo 13 back on its loop around the Moon was built by which company, and what kind of lander was it?
rows.answer: The craft was the lunar module Aquarius, built by Grumman, and it was a two-stage lander. [[lunar-module]] "[stated] Two-stage lander built by Grumman (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The engine that put Apollo 13 back on a free-return path was its descent engine. [[lunar-module]] "[stated] Its descent engine burn put Apollo 13 back on a free-return path (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Grumman's own note also records the build. [[grumman]] "[stated] Built the Apollo lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: Charlie Duke and Gene Kranz both had a role in the same event. Which event, and what was each one's role?
rows.answer:
Both had roles in the Apollo 11 lunar landing. Charlie Duke was capsule communicator during the landing ([[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Was capsule communicator during the Apollo 11 landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"). Gene Kranz was flight director for the landing ([[gene-kranz]] "[stated] Flight director for the Apollo 11 lunar landing (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)").

Both also appear in Apollo 13, with different roles. Kranz's team was on console when the oxygen tank failed ([[gene-kranz]] "[stated] His team was on console when Apollo 13's oxygen tank failed (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"). Duke was Apollo 13's backup lunar module pilot ([[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot for Apollo 13 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"), and his German measles started the crew swap ([[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"). The notes do not say he had a role in the explosion itself, so Apollo 11 is the event where both roles are clearly stated.
